title: The door that permits every tool
goal: {{castAgentId}} at {{castBrand}} is given the standing door demo-all-tools and needs to know what it can do through it.
obstacle: An agent cannot guess a policy. It has to connect, discover the tools and try one before it knows whether the door is useful.
control: The door's policy covers every tool, so discovery lists all 18. The verdict is Allowed, and the evidence shows who the gateway evaluated and why.
say: This is the widest door: 18 tools listed. Everything here is simulated by the lab's own gateway, and the verdict says so.

steps.title: Pick the door
steps.tell: Choose demo-all-tools. The banner at the top says the gateway is simulated; the identity rail shows the identity the simulated gateway evaluates.
steps.say: One door, one policy, one identity being evaluated.
steps.why: A door is a standing endpoint. Which tools it offers is decided by the policy behind it, not by the client.

steps.title: Discover the tools
steps.tell: Run discovery. The verdict reads Allowed and the tool list shows 18 tools.
steps.why: Discovery is the first call a client makes. It already carries a decision.

steps.title: Run a read-only tool
steps.tell: Select list_entitlements and run it with the sample arguments. The verdict is Allowed and the result is labelled as simulated sample data.
steps.say: A permitted tool answers. The sample data is invented by this lab, not read from {{castBrand}}.
steps.why: A result without a label would look like real data. The label is part of the honesty rule.

steps.title: Open the evidence
steps.tell: Open the movie reel and step through the hops. Each hop shows its request, its response and whether the lab checked it (Mock), or only observed or inferred it (Real).
steps.say: Every hop is on the reel, with the exact request and response.
steps.why: In Real a client cannot see the gateway's internal checks, so the lab never claims it did.
